If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative mid-cycle (last 5 days), shift forecast downward by 2–3% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >1.5% from true path, apply a 1.0–1.5% correction in direction of sentiment dominance for mid horizon (8–15 days).
